newsitem.title: USA: Equus's Puerto Rico track commissions up.
newsitem.headline: Equus's Puerto Rico track commissions up.

text.p: Equus Gaming Co LP said Thursday that wagering commissions for El Comandante Race Track in Puerto Rico rose 7.3 percent to $13.3 million for the quarter ended September 30.
The year-ago figure was $12.4 million, the company said. Commissions for the nine months were $43 million, a 4.6 percent increase from $41.1 million a year ago.

The company attributed rising commissions figures to the addition of one race day each week since February. It said the track hosted 65 race days this quarter, compared with 51 in the year-ago period. The track is scheduled to host 257 race days this year, compared with 207 for 1995, Equus said.

Virginia-based Equus has an 82 percent interest in HDA, a Puerto Rican partnership that owns El Comandante. The HDA partnership also owns 50 percent interest in the TELENET network, which broadcasts El Comandante racing, and a 55 percent interest in a company leasing and operating a government-owned race track in the Dominican Republic.
